13/Dated: 23rd August, 2022 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. This revision application is directed against the judgment dated 20.09.2003 passed by learned 5th Additional District and Sessions Judge, Dumka, in Cr. Appeal No. 196 of 1986/ 60 of 2003;
whereby the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 20.08.1986 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Dumka, in O.C.R. No. 185 of 1976 (T.R. No. 902 of 1986 ); whereby the petitioner has been convicted and sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment one year under Section 16 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, has been affirmed and appeal filed by the petitioner was dismissed.

entities.text: 5th Additional District and Sessions Judge, Dumka
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Ms. Shalaka Srivastava, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the learned trial Court and appellate court have erred in law as well as on facts in passing the impugned judgment.

She further submits that all the prosecution witnesses have made contradictory statements and from the materials brought on record, it is apparent that the prosecution has failed to prove the charge leveled against the petitioner and as per the record, no case is made out against the petitioner.
She further submits that the court below failed to consider that the District Board is not a local authority nor does the district medical officer has any right to sanction.
The analysis was never Mahadeo Dutta vs The State Of Jharkhand.

1 communicated to the petitioner and as a result he was prevented to send the same for the analysis in accordance with law and the same has never been communicated to the accused persons.

She further contended that the appellate Court has not considered the fact that as per PW, the shop of the petitioner is in an open space, and also when the inspection and seizure list was being prepared there was heavy rain and dust which could have affected the quality of black pepper and also it was ceased in wet condition.
The pepper was ceased, the panelist had given a report that it was substandard and no adulteration was recorded.
However, substandard and adulteration are two different things.

She reiterated that no allegation was established, whatsoever, of adulteration of black pepper by the learned trial and appellate court and the complaint itself is not maintainable under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
She lastly submits that the sample of the seized articles was not taken in accordance with the law.

Alternatively, she submits that the instant case is of the year 1976 and about 46 years have elapsed and now the petitioner is about 66 years and he must have suffered mental agony for ongoing litigation and at present.
She further submits that the petitioner has never misused the privilege of bail and he is not a habitual offender, as such some leniency may be granted by this Court.

4. Learned A.P.P. opposes the contention of the petitioner and submits that there is concurrent finding and as such, no interference is required.
5.

After going through the impugned judgments including the lower court records and keeping in mind the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and also the scope of revision jurisdiction, I am not inclined to interfere with the findings of the court below and as such the judgments of conviction passed by the learned trial court and upheld by the learned appellate court is, hereby, sustained.

6. However, so far as sentence is concerned, it is apparent from record that the incident is of the year 1976 and 46 years have elapsed and the petitioner must have suffered the rigors of litigation for the last 46 years.
The petitioner also remained in custody for about 76 days.
Further, it is not stated that the petitioner has ever misused the privilege of bail.
In addition, the incident does not reflect any cruelty on the part of the petitioner or any mental depravity.

7. In a situation of this nature, I am of the opinion that no fruitful purpose would be served by sending the appellant/convict back to prison; rather interest of justice would be sufficed if the sentence is modified to period already undergone.

8. Thus, the sentence passed by the learned trial Court and upheld by the learned appellate Court is hereby modified to the extent that the petitioner is sentenced to undergo for the period already undergone.
Mahadeo Dutta vs The State Of Jharkhand.
